prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at magic twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: I keep B028 alone as the whole prize, and the round-1 exchange has strengthened rather than weakened that view. The chair's question is whether the unsettled pairing mechanism makes the prize premature. I think not, because the citation can be worded around what is reproducible: the flat band at the magic angle that Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011, and the correlated insulating and superconducting states that Jarillo-Herrero's group observed at that angle in 2018 and that many independent groups have since reproduced. The prize would not rest on any pairing theory. Four of us now prefer B028 alone, and all eight ranked it, but I do not treat that count as the argument. The argument is the tight, falsifiable pairing of prediction and experiment, and a platform in which interaction strength is set by angle and gate. On the credited names I keep all three. Bistritzer is the first author of the 2011 paper that named the magic angle, and dropping him would turn a three-name prediction-plus-experiment structure into an arbitrary cut. I would put Cao and the first-author team, and the Dean and Young groups, in the record as an acknowledged limit of the three-name rule, not as a reason to widen the prize.
statement.case_against: The field is under a decade old and the origin of the superconductivity is unresolved, so the committee can legitimately judge the prize early. Twist-angle disorder and strain still produce device-to-device variation. Attribution is imperfect, since Cao and the other first authors fall outside the three names. B022 is cleaner on credit and has stronger independent reproduction, and Kroll and Lindroth are right that the Katori-Ye allocation is easier to defend. My honest weakness is that B028 asks the Academy to accept a platform discovery with a contested interpretation, whereas B022 asks for less. If the committee decides that a young field with open interpretation cannot be recognised this year, I would move to B022 alone and not to a combined configuration, because no pairing that includes B028 fits within three names.

responses.point: Kroll holds that B022 is the cleaner single-achievement choice and that the case does not rest on the pending redefinition of the second, while accepting that the citation must show a distinct step beyond the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
responses.response: I agree that the lattice-clock science is established independently of the redefinition and that Katori and Ye is a clean allocation. I still weigh the overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock prizes more heavily than you do, because the Academy would need to explain why a third precision-atomic prize is a new discovery and not a refinement of accuracy. Your own suggested citation language would help, but it does not remove the overlap. I have not moved on maturity of B028 either: I regard the flat-band and correlated-phase observations as secure, which is the question for a prize. I keep B022 as my first alternative and would not object to it.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that Katori's magic-wavelength lattice is a conceptual step beyond the comb readout tool and the ion-trap platform, and she would not combine B022 with B002 without a joint argument.
responses.response: Your reply to Mehlig persuades me that the lattice clock is more than engineering: the state-insensitive trap is an idea about light shifts and atomic structure, and I withdraw any suggestion that it is merely incremental. I also agree that pairing it with another candidate because of overlapping support would be weak. That is why I would not propose B022 plus B028, which would also need five names. My remaining difference is that B028 opened a new class of correlated phenomena that other fields are now using, while the clock case is strongest as a measurement capability. I accept that this is a judgement about breadth and not a decisive point.

responses.point: Mehlig notes that my first-place opening choice B001 has a still-debated mechanism, so ranking it first applies a different maturity standard than the one used against B028.
responses.response: That is a fair challenge and I accept it. As a microscopist working on LaAlO3/SrTiO3 I know that oxygen vacancies and cation intermixing complicate the carrier story, so I cannot argue that B001 is mature while holding B028 early. That is why I do not carry B001 into my configuration or my alternatives. The difference I would keep is that for B028 the open question is the interpretation of one phase, while the existence and reproducibility of the flat-band correlated regime is not in doubt. For B001 the interface origin of the electron system itself is still contested, which is a more basic uncertainty.

responses.point: Eriksson asked how I weigh oxygen-vacancy and intermixing doubts at LaAlO3/SrTiO3 against his mechanism doubts about twisted bilayer graphene, and treats the Dean group as part of the later field.
responses.response: I weigh them differently because the doubt in B001 concerns what the object is, whereas the doubt in B028 concerns why a well-defined object has the phases it has. I agree with you that Dean's group is better treated as part of the later field than as a missing co-discoverer of the magic-angle effect, and that waiting for the pairing question could take another decade. I also take your point that B048 is narrower than B031. I keep B031 only as a second alternative and would not defend adding Xue, since the quantum anomalous Hall observation is a separate sub-discovery.

responses.point: Johansson moved to B028 for timing and independence, would word the citation around flat bands and correlated phases, and notes that the three-name B028 is harder to defend than a two-person B022.
responses.response: I agree with the wording principle and think the committee should settle it now: the citation names flat bands and correlated insulating and superconducting states, and says nothing about the pairing mechanism. On the allocation, the prediction came seven years before the observation and named the angle, so the three names map onto distinct roles. I accept that B022 is simpler, but simplicity of attribution is not the only criterion. On the Chalmers connection, I note again that we share no project on any shortlisted candidate.

responses.point: Pearce prefers B002 with B022 and says B037 or B028 is the better partner for B022 if Halzen alone cannot carry a part.
responses.response: I do not think B028 should be the partner for B022, because that needs five names and cannot meet the limit of three. On B002 I still want the committee to state why Halzen alone is the decisive credit for a collaboration of hundreds, and I have not heard an argument that settles it. I can accept that IceCube is a real discovery and that your field knowledge is more reliable than mine here. If the committee does not take B028 alone, I would sooner see B022 alone than a paired prize whose second part carries an attribution weakness.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the field mature enough given the unresolved pairing mechanism, even with a citation limited to flat bands and correlated phases.
Whether Bistritzer should be credited alongside MacDonald, and how to acknowledge Cao and the first-author team under the three-name limit.
Whether the clock prize should be preferred because its credit and reproduction are cleaner, which I cannot rule out.
Whether the Academy would prefer to avoid a second condensed-matter materials prize when strong atomic and particle candidates are also available.
statement.conflict_note: I have no documented connection to the B028 candidates. My earlier disclosure stands: I work on LaAlO3/SrTiO3 oxide interfaces by transmission electron microscopy, which is why I discount B001 and do not advocate it. Göran Johansson is also at Chalmers, a documented institutional connection with no shared project on any shortlisted candidate; he has moved away from B014 for his own field reasons and I raise no concern about it. I would not claim any further relationships.
